title: WireGuard: Fast, Simple, and Easy to Block
metaTitle: What Is WireGuard? How It Works and Why It Gets Blocked
metaDescription: WireGuard explained: its fixed modern cryptography, why it is so fast, why its fixed-size handshake makes it easy for censors to block, and which apps use it.
excerpt: The fastest mainstream VPN protocol, with fixed modern cryptography and a tiny codebase. It was never built to hide, and filtered networks block it first.

faq.question: Is WireGuard secure?
faq.answer: Yes. WireGuard uses a fixed set of modern primitives (ChaCha20-Poly1305, Curve25519, BLAKE2s) and has a small codebase that is practical to audit. Its weakness is visibility to censors, not the strength of its encryption.

faq.question: Why does WireGuard stop working in Russia or Iran?
faq.answer: Its handshake messages have fixed sizes, 148 bytes from the client and 92 bytes in reply, over UDP. That pattern is simple for deep packet inspection to detect, and carriers in Russia have been reported cutting WireGuard sessions right after the handshake.

faq.question: Is WireGuard faster than OpenVPN?
faq.answer: Usually, yes. WireGuard sets up a session in one round trip, runs in the kernel on Linux, and has far less protocol overhead to negotiate. The exact difference depends on the device and network.

faq.question: Can WireGuard be hidden from DPI?
faq.answer: Not on its own. Forks such as AmneziaWG change packet sizes and headers to make the traffic less recognisable, or WireGuard can be wrapped inside another protocol, at some cost in speed.
